narrative: Material PL1__MBA306AC exhibits erratic daily demand (CV=0.23) averaging 1,025 units/day across 216 working days, with a slight downward trend and 6 outliers winsorised at bounds of 411 and 1,496 units. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.67, range 0.28–3.88 days), making lead-time variability the dominant driver of the 1,553-unit safety stock requirement at 95% service level. The EOQ of 8,159 units is hard-capped to 4,016 units by the 5,570-unit storage limit, resulting in more frequent ordering every ~4 days. The current SAP policy holds zero safety stock and an oversized order quantity, creating material stockout exposure that the (r,Q) policy directly addresses.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint is binding: EOQ 8159 capped to 4016 to satisfy max_storage_units=5569.651 with safety_stock=1553.
Capacity utilisation at replenishment peak is 99.99% — any safety stock increase requires physical storage expansion.
Slight downward demand trend detected (slope=-1.30 units/day); monitor for continued decline.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Continuous-review (r,Q) is appropriate for high-frequency, non-zero daily demand with unstable lead times. The fixed order quantity respects the MOQ=347 and storage cap, while the reorder point provides a dynamic trigger that absorbs lead-time uncertainty. A periodic-review model would be less responsive given the unstable lead-time variability.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage cap binds tightly (99.99% utilisation at replenishment peak: 1553+4016=5569 vs limit 5569.651). Any demand upside or rounding increase in safety stock could breach capacity. Service level is constrained by physical storage — to achieve higher than 95% SL, storage must be expanded first.
research_insights.escalation_flag: No MOQ-capacity infeasibility: MOQ(347)+safety_stock(1553)=1900 < max_storage_units(5569.651). Constraint is satisfied. Monitor capacity utilisation closely given near-zero headroom of 0.65 units.
